localOperationalNotes: In Madison, university referrals should be reflected in the clinic risk analysis, not left as informal knowledge held by one administrator.

operatingPriorities: Confirm each PHI-handling vendor has a signed BAA before Madison staff use it for patient-specific work.
Define how referrals, consult notes, imaging requests, and outside records move between clinic staff and specialty partners.
Review shared inboxes, fax alternatives, and task tools used by referral coordinators.
Run a security risk analysis that covers remote work, backups, device loss, and cloud tools.
Use the cited Wisconsin source as a refresh trigger for current state healthcare oversight materials.
evidenceCadence: Weekly: review open specialty referrals tasks for patient-identifying details in task names, comments, inboxes, attachments, and reminders.
Monthly: sample vendor, access, training, and incident records for Madison workflows and confirm each item has an owner, due date, status, and retained evidence.

Quarterly: refresh the risk analysis sections tied to referral documentation, specialist access, care-coordination tasks, and vendor boundaries, then document what changed and which staff examples need retraining.
Annually: compare the clinic's HIPAA policies against current federal sources and the cited Wisconsin source before approving the next training cycle.
softwareBuyingCriteria: Require a BAA before Madison staff enter PHI into scheduling, messaging, billing, analytics, AI, storage, form, or task-management software.
Prefer tools that keep PHI out of email notifications, calendar titles, exported task names, analytics tags, and AI prompts unless those surfaces are explicitly covered.

Confirm the product can preserve evidence for referral documentation, specialist access, care-coordination tasks, and vendor boundaries: owner, due date, completion status, review notes, attachments, and change history.
Avoid buying a broad project-management system for Madison compliance work unless the clinic can prove BAA scope, admin settings, retention, audit exports, and staff training boundaries.

Verify BAAs for referral, imaging, fax, task-management, billing, and records-request vendors before PHI use.
Train workforce members on minimum necessary access, patient identity checks, and incident escalation.

faq.q: What is the fastest HIPAA starting point for a Madison clinic?
faq.a: Start with a current risk analysis, a vendor/BAA inventory, workforce training records, and documented rules for patient messaging, referrals, billing follow-up, and records requests.

faq.q: Does Wisconsin replace HIPAA for Madison clinics?
faq.a: No. HIPAA remains the federal baseline for covered entities and business associates. Madison clinics should check current Wisconsin materials before changing workflows because state oversight, medical-record, privacy, or incident expectations can change.

faq.q: Which vendors should a Madison clinic review first?
faq.a: Review vendors that touch PHI first, especially referral, imaging, fax, task-management, billing, and records-request vendors. Confirm the workflow is allowed, the right plan or contract is in place, and a BAA is signed before PHI use.

faq.q: How often should a Madison clinic review HIPAA evidence?
faq.a: Review high-change workflows monthly, run a broader evidence review quarterly, and refresh policies and training at least annually. Add extra reviews after vendor, staffing, location, or patient communication changes.
